title: Searching for axion dark matter conversion spectral lines in neutron star magnetospheres with FAST
summary: The axion is a well-motivated dark matter candidate, which can convert into narrow radio spectral lines via the Primakoff effect in the strongly magnetized magnetospheres of neutron stars. This provides a novel astrophysical probe for axion searches that is complementary to laboratory experiments. Using FAST, the world's most sensitive single-dish radio telescope, we observed two X-ray dim isolated neutron stars (RXJ1605.3+3249 and RXJ1308.6+2127) within its sky coverage, which are predicted to yield the strongest axion-conversion spectral lines (ACL). Although no significant signal was detected at the 5 sigma confidence level, we establish new upper limits on the axion-photon coupling constant g_{a gamma gamma} less than or similar to 5 x 10^{-12} GeV^{-1} for axion masses ranging from 4.14 to 6.20 micro-eV corresponding to the 1.0-1.5 GHz observational band. This result constitutes the tightest constraint in this axion mass range among all existing studies employing the same ACL-based method.

AI.tldr: This paper uses FAST to search for axion dark matter signals from neutron star magnetospheres, setting the strongest current limits on axion-photon coupling for axion masses of 4.14–6.20 μeV despite no detection.
AI.motivation: To search for axion dark matter via its conversion to narrow radio spectral lines in neutron star magnetospheres, providing a novel astrophysical probe complementing laboratory experiments.
AI.method: Used the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Telescope (FAST) to observe two X-ray dim isolated neutron stars predicted to produce strong axion-conversion spectral lines via the Primakoff effect.
AI.result: No significant axion-conversion signal was detected at 5 sigma confidence level; set new upper limits on the axion-photon coupling constant g_{aγγ} ≤ 5 × 10^{-12} GeV^{-1} for axion masses between 4.14 and 6.20 μeV.
AI.conclusion: The study places the most stringent constraints to date on the axion-photon coupling constant in the specified mass range using axion-conversion spectral lines from neutron stars, advancing astrophysical searches for axion dark matter.

title: What an Amortized X-ray Posterior Cannot See: Gain Shifts, Silent Miscalibration, and Where Nested Sampling Still Earns Its Cost
comment: 6 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/WizardEternal/sbi-xray-calibration
summary: Neural posterior estimation (NPE) gives X-ray spectral fits a posterior in milliseconds instead of the minutes nested sampling costs, but without its calibration guarantee or goodness-of-fit. The simulation-based inference (SBI) literature has trust diagnostics for this gap that have not been benchmarked on X-ray spectra. We provide the first such benchmark on one real XMM-Newton EPIC-pn response: a 5-parameter absorbed continuum across three count regimes (~100, 1000, 10000 counts), four misspecification families, and nested sampling on the exact Poisson likelihood as reference. A posterior-predictive check catches an unmodeled 6.4 keV line (ROC AUC 0.97 above ~1000 counts), where a missed line biases the photon index by +0.20 at bright counts. A 3% detector gain shift stays at chance (AUC ~0.50, 36 cells) for all three per-spectrum scores while distorting the continuum; only nested sampling's evidence flags it (Delta log Z ~ -7.8 at medium counts). Separately, one flow passed every recovery check yet was miscalibrated (marginal coverage deviation 0.113); reseeds and an uncapped retrain trace this to single-flow undertraining, not the count regime, and split-conformal repaired it (0.113 -> 0.026). Recovery metrics do not certify calibration, and a fast amortized posterior still needs an evidence-based check in the loop.

AI.tldr: This paper benchmarks trust diagnostics for neural posterior estimation in X-ray spectral fitting, revealing that posterior-predictive checks and evidence evaluation reliably detect model misspecifications and miscalibration, which recovery metrics might miss. Fast inference methods need ongoing evidence-based validation to ensure accurate and calibrated posterior estimates.
AI.motivation: To address the lack of calibration guarantees and goodness-of-fit checks for neural posterior estimation (NPE) applied to X-ray spectral fits, which is faster than nested sampling but less reliable without trust diagnostics.
AI.method: Benchmarking simulation-based inference (SBI) trust diagnostics on an XMM-Newton EPIC-pn X-ray response using a 5-parameter absorbed continuum model across multiple count regimes, misspecification families, and nested sampling on exact Poisson likelihood as the reference. Employing posterior-predictive checks, evidence evaluation, recovery checks, and split-conformal methods.
AI.result: Posterior-predictive checks effectively detect unmodeled spectral features (6.4 keV line) with high accuracy (ROC AUC 0.97) at sufficient counts, highlighting bias in photon index due to missed lines. Detector gain shifts remain undetected by per-spectrum scores but are flagged by nested sampling evidence. Recovery checks can pass despite miscalibration due to single-flow undertraining, which retraining and split-conformal correction ameliorate. Recovery metrics alone cannot guarantee calibration; evidence-based checks remain necessary in fast amortized posteriors.
AI.conclusion: While neural posterior estimation accelerates X-ray spectral fitting significantly, it lacks inherent calibration guarantees and can miss critical spectral features or miscalibrations. Trust diagnostics like posterior-predictive checks and evidence evaluation are essential for validating these fast inference methods. Recovery metrics alone are insufficient, and maintaining evidence-based monitoring is crucial to ensure reliable posterior estimates in X-ray spectral analysis.

title: Constraints on Late-Time Flaring from Luminous Fast Blue Optical Transients using the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite and the Zwicky Transient Facility
comment: 23 pages (including references), 8 figures, 6 tables. Submitted to ApJ
summary: The Luminous Fast Blue Optical Transient (LFBOT) AT2022tsd exhibited minutes-timescale optical flares in the tens of days following the initial transient event, likely due to a central engine -- either an accreting black hole or a magnetar. In this paper, we use data from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) and the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) to constrain the occurrence of similar flares in the 12 (of 14) known LFBOTs that had observational coverage with TESS from tens of days to thousands of days after the transient's initial emission. We find seven flare-like signals at the locations of four unique LFBOTs; all seven can likely be attributed to a solar system object (SSO) moving through the TESS aperture. Assuming all seven flares arise from SSOs, for the LFBOT AT2024qfm we rule out flaring with a similar timescale (40--65 d) and luminosity ($νL_ν\sim10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$) as in AT2022tsd, while for AT2022tsd itself we rule out flares between 380--430 d after the initial transient that were as luminous as the earlier flares. This observation suggests that the engine power in AT2022tsd declined or shut off on a timescale of hundreds of days. We also find that there is no late-time activity detectable in TESS thousands of days after the prototype LFBOT, AT2018cow. We discuss our constraints on the duty cycle of such flaring and then present estimates for the number of minutes-duration flares detectable with ongoing and upcoming high-cadence ($\ll1$ d) wide-field surveys.

AI.tldr: This study used TESS and ZTF observations to search for minutes-timescale optical flares in 12 LFBOTs, finding no intrinsic flares except in AT2022tsd where flaring ceased within hundreds of days. The engine powering these flares appears to decline over time, with implications for future high-cadence transient surveys.
AI.motivation: To investigate the presence and characteristics of optical flares in Luminous Fast Blue Optical Transients (LFBOTs), specifically to determine if minutes-timescale optical flares similar to those observed in AT2022tsd occur in other LFBOTs and to constrain the flaring activity and engine power timeline.
AI.method: Utilized observational data from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) and the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) to search for and analyze minute-timescale optical flares in 12 well-covered LFBOTs. Identified flare-like signals and assessed their origin, ruling out solar system object contamination for certain events. Conducted temporal flare activity analysis to constrain engine power duration and duty cycle estimates.
AI.result: Seven flare-like signals detected at four LFBOT locations likely caused by solar system objects, leading to constraints on flare occurrence in LFBOTs. For AT2024qfm, flares similar to AT2022tsd were ruled out within a 40–65 day window post-transient. For AT2022tsd, luminous flares were absent 380–430 days after the initial event, suggesting engine power decline or cessation over hundreds of days. No late-time flare activity detected in AT2018cow thousands of days post-transient. Estimates provided for detectability of similar flares in future high-cadence surveys.
AI.conclusion: The central engine powering optical flares in LFBOT AT2022tsd likely declines or shuts off within hundreds of days post-transient, as similar flaring activity was not observed in other LFBOTs or at late times in AT2022tsd and AT2018cow. This constrains the duty cycle and longevity of such flaring activity and informs expectations for future detections in ongoing and upcoming surveys.

title: Optical polarization variability and its relation to gamma-ray activity in blazars
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics. Manuscript no. aa60588-26. 5 pages, 4 figures
summary: Optical polarization can be an important probe of particle acceleration and high-energy emission processes in relativistic jets from supermassive black holes. We combined publicly available observations from three past blazar monitoring programs to produce densely sampled light curves for 15 blazars in order to explore the relation of gamma-ray activity to the polarization variability as well as discover new rotations of the polarization angle. We find that the polarization degree does not correlate with the gamma-ray flux for individual sources nor different subsamples of blazars, potentially indicating multiple emission mechanisms. In the combined dataset, we identified a total of 64 rotations in 12 sources, 39 of which are newly identified rotations. We confirm the trend found in previous works for the whole sample: lower polarization degrees during periods of polarization angle rotations. However, looking at the individual sources, we identified cases where the rotation and non-rotation polarization degree distributions are indistinguishable, providing further evidence for the multiple emission mechanism hypothesis.

AI.tldr: This study combined data from 15 blazars to analyze optical polarization and gamma-ray activity, discovering 64 polarization angle rotations and evidence suggesting multiple emission mechanisms due to varying polarization correlations with gamma-ray flux.
AI.motivation: To investigate the relationship between gamma-ray activity and optical polarization variability in relativistic jets of supermassive black holes, and to discover new rotations of the polarization angle in blazars.
AI.method: Combined and analyzed publicly available optical polarization data from three blazar monitoring programs to produce densely sampled light curves for 15 blazars, identifying polarization angle rotations and studying correlations with gamma-ray flux.
AI.result: Identified 64 polarization angle rotations in 12 blazars (39 newly discovered), found no correlation between polarization degree and gamma-ray flux in individual sources or blazar subsamples, and confirmed lower polarization degrees during rotation periods for the whole sample. However, some individual sources showed no difference in polarization degree distributions between rotation and non-rotation periods.
AI.conclusion: The findings support the hypothesis of multiple emission mechanisms in blazar jets, as polarization behavior and its relation to gamma-ray activity varies across sources and conditions.

title: Hawai`i Supernova Flows: Bulk Flow Measurements using SNe Ia in the Optical and NIR
comment: 20 pages, 7 figures. All code available at https://github.com/ado8/hsf_bulkflows
summary: The present day peculiar velocity-field was sourced by primordial density fluctuations and sculpted over the lifespan of the Universe. Cosmological models such as $Λ$CDM make predictions for various statistical properties of peculiar velocities. Bulk flow, the average velocity within a given volume, has an expectation value of $\vec{0}$ due to isotropy, and a variance directly tied to the Hubble constant, the growth-rate of structure, and the matter power spectrum. In this paper, we use the redshifts and optical and near-infrared distance estimates to Type Ia Supernovae (SNe Ia) within subsets of the Hawai`i Supernova Flows dataset to infer the bulk flow within $z \lesssim 0.1$. The inferred speeds vary between ~100 to 400 km/s but are all consistent with the predictions of $Λ$CDM. As a secondary focus, we discuss the systematic uncertainty introduced by the discrete choice of methodology using two bulk flow estimators, two types of SN Ia distance estimators, and data covering two distinct regimes in wavelength space.

AI.tldr: This study measured the bulk flow of nearby Type Ia Supernovae using multiple methods and datasets, confirming ΛCDM predictions and discussing systematic uncertainties from measurement techniques.
AI.motivation: To test cosmological model predictions on peculiar velocity fields using observational data, improving understanding of Universe's structure formation.
AI.method: Used redshifts and optical/near-infrared distance estimates of Type Ia Supernovae from the Hawai`i Supernova Flows dataset, applying two bulk flow estimators and two types of SN Ia distance estimators across different wavelength regimes to infer bulk flow at low redshift (z<0.1).
AI.result: Bulk flow speeds inferred range from ~100 to 400 km/s, consistent with ΛCDM predictions; noted systematic uncertainties arising from methodology and data choices.
AI.conclusion: The measured bulk flows within low-redshift volumes agree with ΛCDM cosmological expectations, validating model predictions for peculiar velocity statistics, while highlighting methodological systematics in bulk flow estimation.

title: QPO-like Signatures and Hydrodynamical Variability in Accretion around a JNW-type Compact Spacetime in Freund-Nambu Scalar-Tensor Gravity
comment: 11 pages, 4 figures, 1 Table
summary: Scalar tensor theories of gravity provide a broad as well as physically rich extension of general theory of relativity by allowing the gravitational interaction to be mediated not only by the spacetime metric but also by scalar degrees of freedom. In this manuscript, we present a new exact solution in the Freund-Nambu scalar-tensor (FNST) gravity scenario, representing a nontrivial scalar-tensor generalization of the Janis-Newman-Winicour naked-singularity geometry, characterized by an additional coupling parameter q in the scalar sector. We also numerically solve the general relativistic hydrodynamic equations in order to investigate the shock-cone mechanism formed by Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion around this compact spacetime on the equatorial plane. We show that stronger scalar-tensor deviations modify the shock-cone morphology, significantly increase the amount of matter accumulated near the central compact object, and enhance the oscillatory behavior of the shock cone. The Lorentzian-like peaks obtained from the numerically computed power spectral density are interpreted as hydrodynamically generated QPO-like modes. These modes are driven by shock cone oscillations and by the compression and rarefaction of the plasma trapped inside the cone. Finally, for a compact object with mass parameter M = 10M_sun, the numerically extracted frequencies are found mainly in the range from a few Hz up to approximately 100 Hz. These frequencies overlap with the QPO ranges reported in stellar-mass black-hole-candidate systems. In particular, the frequencies obtained for the FNST2-FNST4 models fall within the range of timing features reported for the source GRS 1915+105. These results suggest that the exterior hydrodynamical variability of FNST compact spacetimes may provide phenomenological diagnostics of scalar-field-induced deviations from the Schwarzschild reference case.

AI.tldr: Presented a new scalar-tensor gravity solution and showed via numerical hydrodynamics that scalar-field effects modify shock cones around compact objects, producing QPO-like oscillations with frequencies matching observed signals in black-hole candidates, offering a way to detect deviations from general relativity.
AI.motivation: To explore scalar-tensor gravity as an extension of general relativity and investigate observable effects of scalar fields around compact objects.
AI.method: Derived a new exact solution in the Freund-Nambu scalar-tensor gravity representing a generalization of a naked-singularity geometry, and performed numerical simulations of general relativistic hydrodynamics to analyze shock-cone formation via Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion.
AI.result: Stronger scalar-tensor deviations alter shock-cone morphology, increase matter accumulation, enhance oscillations leading to hydrodynamically generated QPO-like modes with frequencies comparable to observed QPOs in stellar-mass black-hole candidates, specifically matching ranges seen in GRS 1915+105.
AI.conclusion: The study demonstrates that scalar-tensor deviations in gravity can produce distinct hydrodynamic variability signatures near compact objects, which may serve as diagnostics to detect scalar-field-induced gravitational effects beyond Schwarzschild geometry.

title: Tracing Ultra Light Axions in Post-reionization, Lyman-$α$ and CMB Missions
comment: 12 sets of figures. 2 tables. Comments are welcome!
summary: Ultra-light axions (ULAs) are dark matter candidates proposed to resolve the small scale anomalies of the standard cosmological model. Due to their inherent quantum pressure, ULAs result in a distinct, scale-dependent suppression on the matter power spectrum, which can leave imprints on the upcoming observations. We explore such possibilities by forecasting on the post-reionization large scale structure (LSS) surveys and next-generation cosmic microwave background (CMB) missions. By utilizing the cross-correlation between 21-cm intensity mapping (SKA1-MID and PUMA) and the Lyman-$α$ forest (DESI-like), we explore possible signatures of ULAs in post-reionization surveys while mitigating instrument-specific systematics. The Fisher matrix analysis projects uncertainties on the fractional ULA abundance across a wide ULA mass range of $10^{-30}\text{ eV} \le m_a \le 10^{-20}\text{ eV}$, revealing an optimal detection sensitivity at intermediate masses around $m_a \sim 10^{-25}\text{ eV}$. Furthermore, while next-generation CMB mission alone can yield small projected errors on the ULA fraction compared to future LSS missions, a joint analysis of the DESI-like and PUMA cross-spectrum alongside CMB-S4-like missions estimates an error on the ULA fraction to be $\mathcal{O}(10^{-4})$ for $m_a\lesssim 10^{-28}$ eV, highlighting a significant improvement over standalone LSS and CMB missions.

AI.tldr: This paper forecasts that combining 21-cm intensity mapping, Lyman-alpha forest, and next-generation CMB observations will notably improve constraints on ultra-light axion dark matter, especially around masses of 10^{-25} eV, achieving high sensitivity beyond individual surveys.
AI.motivation: To investigate the potential of upcoming post-reionization large scale structure surveys and next-generation CMB missions in detecting ultra-light axions (ULAs), which may explain small scale anomalies in cosmology.
AI.method: Forecasting using Fisher matrix analysis on the cross-correlation between 21-cm intensity mapping (SKA1-MID and PUMA) and Lyman-alpha forest (DESI-like) data, combined with next-generation CMB mission data.
AI.result: The analysis predicts optimal ULA detection sensitivity at masses around 10^{-25} eV; joint analysis of LSS and CMB data improves fractional ULA abundance constraints to the order of 10^{-4} for masses below 10^{-28} eV, surpassing standalone survey capabilities.
AI.conclusion: Cross-correlating multiple observational probes such as 21-cm intensity mapping and Lyman-alpha forest, combined with next-generation CMB data, significantly enhances the ability to detect or constrain ULAs across a wide mass range, providing a powerful method to test dark matter models involving ULAs.

title: Discovery of a Supernova Following the Einstein Probe Transient EP250302a at z = 1.131
comment: Submitted to ApJ
summary: We present a multi-wavelength analysis of the Einstein Probe (EP) fast X-ray transient (FXT) EP250302a located at redshift $z=1.131$. Despite its luminous prompt X-ray emission, the event was not detected in gamma-rays. Multi-wavelength follow-up identified a bright optical and X-ray source that displayed rapid chromatic flaring before returning to the standard decay of a gamma-ray burst afterglow. We interpret the chromatic flare as either due to a refreshed shock caused by a discrete shell collision or as reverse shock emission. Using the early optical data, we place constraints on the Lorentz factor of the outflow, requiring an ultrarelativistic jet with $Γ_0>25$. We additionally obtained deep late-time imaging with the Gemini North Telescope that reveals the presence of an optical excess at $20-30$ d post-explosion. We interpret this as supernova (SN) emission and find good agreement with the canonical broad-lined Ic SN 1998bw with a flux-scaling factor of $k_\textrm{98bw}>0.3$. This adds to the growing evidence that the majority of EP FXTs are associated with the deaths of massive stars.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the X-ray transient EP250302a at redshift 1.131, finding it involves ultrarelativistic jets and shows supernova-like optical emission, supporting its origin from massive star death.
AI.motivation: To understand the nature and origin of the Einstein Probe fast X-ray transient EP250302a and to clarify its association with massive star deaths.
AI.method: Multi-wavelength observations including X-ray, optical follow-up, and deep late-time imaging with Gemini North were used to analyze the transient's emission properties and temporal behavior.
AI.result: The event showed rapid chromatic flaring interpreted as refreshed or reverse shocks, required an ultrarelativistic jet with Lorentz factor >25, and exhibited late-time optical excess consistent with a broad-lined Ic supernova similar to SN 1998bw.
AI.conclusion: The study supports that EP fast X-ray transients like EP250302a are linked to massive star deaths and involve ultrarelativistic jets and supernova emissions.

title: Damped Harmonic Oscillator Dark Energy and the Hubble Tension
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures, All comments are welcome
summary: We investigate a dark-energy equation of state governed by a damped harmonic oscillator equation, admitting underdamped, critically damped, and overdamped solutions. Confronting the model against Planck CMB, DESI BAO, BBN, Cosmic Chronometers, and three Type~Ia supernova compilations, we find that the underdamped solution yields $H_0 = 70.9 \pm 1.1$ km/s/Mpc, with DESY5 and $H_0 = 72.0^{+1.4}_{-2.1}$ km/s/Mpc with Union3, reducing the tension with SH0ES to $\sim\!1.4σ$, while Pantheon+ strongly favors a near-critically damped solution with positive $w_0$ and $H_0 = 66.23 \pm 0.85$ km/s/Mpc, revealing a significant systematic tension among supernova datasets. Bayesian evidence relative to $Λ$CDM is inconclusive for DES and Union3 data, demonstrating that $H_0$ tension alleviation is achievable at no statistical cost relative to the standard model.

AI.tldr: A dark-energy equation of state modeled by a damped harmonic oscillator can reduce the Hubble constant tension with no statistical cost compared to $Λ$CDM, but significant systematic differences remain among supernova datasets.
AI.motivation: Address the tension in measurements of the Hubble constant ($H_0$) by proposing an alternative dark-energy equation of state model.
AI.method: Model the dark-energy equation of state using a damped harmonic oscillator equation, allowing for underdamped, critically damped, and overdamped solutions; confront these models with multiple cosmological datasets including Planck CMB, DESI BAO, BBN, Cosmic Chronometers, and three Type Ia supernova compilations.
AI.result: The underdamped solution yields values of $H_0$ (~70.9 and 72.0 km/s/Mpc) that reduce the tension with SH0ES data to about 1.4 sigma for two supernova datasets (DESY5 and Union3). Pantheon+ dataset favors a near-critically damped solution with a lower $H_0$ (~66.23 km/s/Mpc), indicating a significant systematic tension among supernova datasets. Bayesian evidence indicates that $H_0$ tension alleviation can be achieved with these models without statistical cost relative to the standard $Λ$CDM model.
AI.conclusion: The damped harmonic oscillator dark-energy model can alleviate the $H_0$ tension satisfactorily for certain datasets, although discrepancies among supernova compilations persist; this model offers a viable alternative to $Λ$CDM without loss of statistical fit.

title: The properties of tidal disruption event infrared counterparts produced by dust rings and inference of the observing angle
comment: 8 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables. Accepted to MNRAS
summary: A substantial fraction of tidal disruption events (TDEs), resulting from a black holes's disruption and accretion of a star, exhibit infrared (IR) counterparts thought to arise from spherical shells of dust reprocessing the TDE emission. Some modelling of TDEs also predicts an angular dependence in their observed properties with more X-ray emission on-axis and more optical emission at higher angles. However, there is growing evidence that X-ray rich TDEs are more likely to exhibit IR counterparts, contradicting the spherical shell model that predicts no significant variation in IR luminosity with angle. Here, I demonstrate that this result naturally follows for dust arranged in a ring instead of a spherical shell. I present a toy model of this scenario and show that on-axis angles result in a brighter counterpart. I also show that on-axis angles result in a delay in the initial rise and off-axis angles may display a double-peaked structure. Crucially, this model also allows the observing angle of the TDE to be constrained. Finally, I demonstrate that this model reproduces the properties of two IR counterparts, including constraining their observing angles and independently inferring an optical plateau, and briefly comment on its application to quasi-periodic eruption counterparts.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a ring-shaped dust model around tidal disruption events to explain observed infrared emission's angular dependence, reproducing key features and enabling constraints on observing angles, unlike spherical shell models.
AI.motivation: There is a discrepancy between existing spherical shell dust models of TDE infrared emission and observational evidence showing X-ray rich TDEs more likely have IR counterparts, implying angular dependence in IR luminosity.
AI.method: The paper develops a toy model where dust is arranged in a ring rather than a spherical shell around the TDE, analyzing how viewing angles affect IR counterpart brightness, timing, and light curve structure.
AI.result: The ring dust model explains why X-ray rich TDEs have brighter IR counterparts on-axis, predicts light curve features such as delayed onset and double peaks depending on angle, allows constraint of observing angles, and reproduces properties of two observed IR counterparts.
AI.conclusion: Dust geometry arranged in a ring rather than a spherical shell naturally explains the observed angular dependence of IR counterparts in TDEs, allowing for improved interpretation of multi-wavelength observations and constraining viewing angles.

title: Joint reconstruction of $H(z)$ and $fσ_8(z)$ with physics informed neural networks
comment: 22 pages; 7 figures
summary: We present a proof of concept for the joint reconstruction of the Hubble parameter $H(z)$ that assumes no dark energy equation of state and the growth rate of large scale structure $fσ_8(z)$ using a physics informed neural network. Rather than fitting these two observables separately and checking their consistency post hoc, we couple them through the linear growth equation of general relativity directly during training, using the equation residual evaluated at collocation points via automatic differentiation as an additional loss term. The network employs a shared backbone feeding two independent output heads, one per observable. We train an ensemble of 100 independently seeded networks on a compilation of 50 $H(z)$ measurements from Cosmic Chronometers and Baryon Acoustic Oscillations and 63 $fσ_8(z)$ measurements from Redshift Space Distortions, and study four values of the physics coupling weight $λ\in \{0,\,0.01,\,0.1,\,1.0\}$. We then anchor the $H_0$ normalization using two independent local distance scale determinations: the SH0ES result $H_0 = 73.04 \pm 1.04$\,km\,s$^{-1}$\,Mpc$^{-1}$ and the Local Distance Network consensus $H_0 = 73.50 \pm 0.81$\,km\,s$^{-1}$\,Mpc$^{-1}$. With either prior the Hubble constant is recovered exactly at the prior value, and the two reconstructions are indistinguishable in $fσ_8(z)$. The reconstructed $fσ_8(z)$ sits systematically below the $Λ$CDM prediction at all redshifts, consistent with the $σ_8$ tension, while the $\mathrm{Om}(z)$ null test shows a marked departure from the flat $Λ$CDM expectation at low redshift. The results establish that coupling the two observables through the growth equation during training is both feasible and beneficial, and that the reconstruction is robust to the choice between the two local $H_0$ determinations.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates a physics informed neural network approach to jointly reconstruct H(z) and fσ8(z) by embedding the linear growth equation during training. The method yields accurate H0 estimates and reveals deviations from ΛCDM predictions, confirming cosmological tensions in a robust manner.
AI.motivation: To jointly reconstruct the Hubble parameter H(z) and the growth rate of large scale structure fσ8(z) without assuming a dark energy equation of state, ensuring consistency between these observables by leveraging physical constraints during training.
AI.method: A physics informed neural network with a shared backbone and two output heads, trained on observational data for H(z) and fσ8(z). The network incorporates the linear growth equation from general relativity as an additional loss term via automatic differentiation, coupling the two observables directly during training. Multiple ensemble networks were trained with varying weights for the physics coupling term.
AI.result: The Hubble constant H0 was accurately recovered at the prior values from two independent local distance scale measurements. The reconstructed fσ8(z) lies systematically below the ΛCDM prediction, supporting the σ8 tension, while the Om(z) null test reveals deviations from flat ΛCDM at low redshift. The coupling of observables during training improved reconstruction and yielded robust results independent of the choice of H0 prior.
AI.conclusion: Coupling H(z) and fσ8(z) through the growth equation within a physics informed neural network framework is feasible and advantageous, producing robust reconstructions consistent with observational data and highlighting tensions with the ΛCDM model.

title: Can a Slow and Strong Phase Transition in Neutron Stars Relieve Major Compact-Star Observation Tensions?
comment: 11 pages, 8 figures
summary: Recent anomalous compact-star observations challenge the conventional neutron-star interpretation in complementary ways: HESS J1731--347 and XTE J1814--338 favor unusually small radii at low mass, while the secondary component of GW190814 appears too massive for an ordinary neutron star under GW170817-based maximum-mass inferences. We examine whether neutron stars with a strong first-order hadron--quark phase transition can address these tensions via the extended stable hybrid branches that arise when the phase conversion is slow compared to radial oscillations, while remaining consistent with GW170817 and NICER constraints. Using a piecewise-polytropic (PP) benchmark, supplemented by an independent speed-of-sound (CS) parametrization comparison, we find two viable patterns in a general parameter scan over both the hadronic and hybrid branches. Scenario 1 realizes an all-at-once solution: the same EOS has a pure hadronic branch compatible with both the GW190814-scale mass and HESS J1731--347, while its slow stable hybrid branch reaches XTE J1814--338. Scenario 2 retains the GW190814-scale hadronic branch but reaches XTE J1814--338 and HESS J1731--347 on slow stable branches in different transition-strength regimes.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that neutron stars with strong hadron-quark phase transitions and slow phase conversion can resolve conflicting observational constraints on neutron star masses and radii, consistent with current gravitational wave and X-ray data.
AI.motivation: Recent anomalous observations of compact stars challenge the conventional neutron star models, as different data suggest contradictory constraints on neutron star radii and masses.
AI.method: The paper examines neutron star models with a strong first-order hadron-quark phase transition, using a piecewise-polytropic benchmark and an independent speed-of-sound parametrization, performing a general parameter scan over hadronic and hybrid branches.
AI.result: Two viable scenarios emerge: Scenario 1 provides a single EOS that accounts for all observations via pure hadronic and slow stable hybrid branches; Scenario 2 accommodates observations by different slow stable hybrid branches associated with varying transition strengths.
AI.conclusion: Neutron stars with strong hadron-quark phase transitions and slow phase conversion can explain the conflicting compact-star observations while remaining consistent with GW170817 and NICER constraints, offering a solution to the tensions in neutron star mass and radius measurements.

title: Synergy between CSST and future gravitational-wave detectors: Probing primordial black holes by cross-correlating dark sirens with galaxies
comment: 13 pages, 5 figures
summary: Gravitational-wave (GW) events and galaxies both trace the cosmic matter distribution, but the mergers of astrophysical black holes and primordial black holes (PBHs) are expected to populate different environments and therefore to cluster with different biases. The GW clustering bias is thus a statistical observable that can separate the two populations. We assess how well this can be done by cross-correlating the photometric galaxy survey of the Chinese Space-station Survey Telescope (CSST) with mock GW catalogs from two future detector networks: the third-generation ET2CE network (the Einstein Telescope and two Cosmic Explorer detectors) and the multi-band BDET2CE network, which adds the space-based baseline Decihertz Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory. We find that CSST combined with 10 years of ET2CE observations can reveal a PBH contribution once its fraction in the total merger rate exceeds about $40\%$, while the much sharper sky localization of BDET2CE lowers this threshold to about $20\%$. The improvement comes from recovering the small-scale clustering information that localization errors would otherwise erase. These results show that combining future GW detector networks with CSST galaxy clustering offers a promising and largely independent route to identifying PBHs statistically.

AI.tldr: This study shows that cross-correlating CSST galaxy data with future GW detectors can statistically identify primordial black hole mergers by exploiting their unique clustering biases, with improved detection thresholds using advanced detector networks.
AI.motivation: To distinguish between mergers of astrophysical black holes and primordial black holes (PBHs) by utilizing their different clustering biases in tracing cosmic matter distribution.
AI.method: Cross-correlating photometric galaxy survey data from the Chinese Space-station Survey Telescope (CSST) with mock gravitational-wave (GW) catalogs from future detector networks ET2CE and BDET2CE, analyzing the ability to detect PBH contributions statistically through clustering bias.
AI.result: CSST combined with 10 years of ET2CE can detect PBH contributions if they exceed ~40% of total mergers; BDET2CE's enhanced localization lowers this detection threshold to ~20%, by preserving small-scale clustering information.
AI.conclusion: Combining future GW detector networks with CSST galaxy clustering enables a promising, largely independent statistical identification of PBHs based on distinct clustering biases.

title: GRB 250424A: A Case Study of Energy Injection with Multiwavelength Observations
comment: 24 pages, 10 figures, 3 tables, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We present a comprehensive multiwavelength analysis of the long-duration gamma-ray burst (GRB) 250424A. Our dataset spans from the prompt gamma-ray emission to late-time optical monitoring, including spectra obtained with the Keck 10\,m telescope. We find that the afterglow light curves display a prominent, simultaneous shallow decay phase in both X-ray and optical bands, followed by an achromatic transition to a standard decay regime. The broadband spectral energy distributions are well-modeled by a single power-law function, indicating a common synchrotron origin for the emission across frequencies. We interpret the afterglow evolution within the framework of a relativistic forward shock refreshed by continuous energy injection. This scenario successfully reproduces the observed temporal and spectral behavior, yielding an isotropic equivalent kinetic energy of $E_{\rm K,iso} \approx 5.5 \times 10^{52}$ erg and an injection index of $q\approx 0.34$ in a constant-density circumburst environment. The shallow decay phase is consistent with sustained energy injection lasting $\sim$ 9 ks. Despite the relatively low redshift, late-time optical observations reveal no distinct supernova component; however, our derived upper limits do not strictly rule out the presence of a typical GRB-associated supernova.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes long-duration GRB 250424A across multiple wavelengths, revealing afterglow behavior consistent with synchrotron emission from a relativistic shock refreshed by continuous energy injection. The kinetic energy and injection parameters are constrained, but no definitive supernova signature was detected.
AI.motivation: To understand the emission mechanisms and energy evolution of the long-duration gamma-ray burst GRB 250424A through multiwavelength observations.
AI.method: Comprehensive multiwavelength analysis including prompt gamma-ray emission, late-time optical monitoring, and spectroscopy with the Keck 10m telescope; modeling broadband spectral energy distributions with a single power-law function; interpreting afterglow evolution using a relativistic forward shock model with continuous energy injection.
AI.result: The afterglow light curves feature a simultaneous shallow decay phase in X-ray and optical bands, followed by a standard decay; spectral energy distributions indicate a synchrotron origin; modeling yields an isotropic equivalent kinetic energy of approximately 5.5 × 10^52 erg and energy injection index q≈0.34 in a constant-density environment; energy injection lasts about 9 ks. No distinct supernova was observed, though its presence cannot be conclusively excluded.
AI.conclusion: The observed multiwavelength afterglow evolution of GRB 250424A is well explained by a relativistic forward shock refreshed by sustained energy injection, supporting the synchrotron emission mechanism in a constant-density circumburst medium. Constraints on the presence of a supernova component remain inconclusive due to observational limits.

title: PSZ: The meta-catalogue of Planck Sunyaev-Zeldovich sources
comment: 20 pages + Appendix (12 pages), 36 figures, submitted to A&A
summary: We present the PSZ, a meta-catalogue of 1962 clusters and cluster candidates produced by the Planck Collaboration. The PSZ contains fully-updated validation information for all official Planck catalogue detections, together with redshift estimates for confirmed clusters, with no duplicate entries. The validation is derived from optical and X-ray follow-up campaigns, supplemented by cross-matching with external catalogues with redshift information, and with XMM-Newton archive data. The external catalogues considered include the all-sky X-ray catalogue MCXC-II, the eROSITA X-ray cluster catalogue, the RASS-MCMF and PSZ-MCMF catalogues, and the extended Planck catalogues of Burenin. A total of 281 clusters are newly-confirmed owing to this process; conversely, 262 Planck candidates are invalidated. Of the 1500 confirmed clusters, 274 have updated redshifts, and 278 have newly-assigned redshifts. An MCXC-II counterpart is assigned to 631 clusters, updating the MCXC cross-match published in the Planck catalogues. Differences with the PSZ2 update of Bahk & Hwang are discussed. We further introduce a new, homogeneously-derived mass estimate, corrected for selection effects owing to intrinsic scatter and the properties of the underlying mass function. New posterior probability contours in the $Y_{5R500}-θ_s$ plane are provided for all sources, in addition to the corresponding $M_{500}(z)$ degeneracy curves. PSZ includes both corrected and uncorrected $M_{500}$ values for confirmed clusters. A methodology for cross-identification between catalogues is presented. We show that simple fixed-distance matching is insufficient for this task, and demonstrate the need for additional consistency checks based on mass proxies, redshifts, and distance versus angular size comparisons. The final PSZ comprises 1500 confirmed clusters, 262 noise-dominated detections, and 200 candidates awaiting validation.

AI.tldr: The PSZ meta-catalogue updates and validates 1962 Planck cluster detections, confirming 1500 clusters with improved redshifts and mass estimates, employing multi-wavelength data and advanced cross-matching techniques for enhanced cluster characterization.
AI.motivation: To produce an updated, reliable meta-catalogue of galaxy clusters detected by the Planck satellite, ensuring validated cluster identifications and accurate redshift and mass information.
AI.method: Compilation and validation of Planck cluster detections through optical and X-ray follow-ups; cross-matching with multiple external catalogues and archival data; development of a methodology for robust cross-identification beyond simple positional matching; and derivation of homogeneous mass estimates correcting for selection effects.
AI.result: The PSZ meta-catalogue contains 1962 entries with 1500 confirmed clusters, including 281 newly confirmed and 262 invalidated candidates. Significant updates include new and updated redshifts, improved mass estimates corrected for biases, and comprehensive cross-matching with external catalogues. The catalogue also provides posterior probability contours and degeneracy curves for cluster properties, enhancing cluster characterization.
AI.conclusion: The PSZ represents a thoroughly validated, homogenized meta-catalogue of Planck-detected galaxy clusters with improved cluster confirmation, redshift data, and mass estimates. It addresses shortcomings of previous catalogues by integrating multiple data sources and employing sophisticated cross-identification methods, thus serving as a valuable resource for cluster cosmology and astrophysical studies.

title: Revisiting Disk Winds in Active Galactic Nuclei as an Origin of Cosmic Gamma-ray and Neutrino Backgrounds
comment: 26 pages, 10 figures, 4 tables; accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: The origin of the cosmic neutrino background (CNB) and the cosmic gamma-ray background (CGB) remains uncertain. Accretion disk winds driven by active galactic nuclei (AGNs) have been proposed as possible contributors, but their predicted background levels depend sensitively on poorly constrained wind energetics and ambient densities. We revisit the AGN disk-wind scenario by constructing a lepto-hadronic wind model calibrated with radio and GeV gamma-ray data of nearby Fermi-LAT-detected Seyfert galaxies. In our framework, cosmic rays accelerated both at wind-driven forward and reverse shocks produce synchrotron, external-Compton, and hadronic emission. We also incorporate recent XRISM constraints on wind parameters. Applying our calibrated lepto-hadronic models to an AGN population synthesis model, we find that disk winds contribute at most $\lesssim 5\%$ of the CGB above 10 GeV and $\lesssim 10\%$ of the CNB around 100 TeV, suggesting that they are unlikely to dominate both backgrounds. Finally, we identify nearby Seyfert galaxies hosting ultrafast outflows as promising targets for future TeV gamma-ray and TeV$-$PeV neutrino observations, which would offer firm tests of the disk-wind scenario.

AI.tldr: This study models AGN disk winds and finds they contribute minimally to cosmic neutrino and gamma-ray backgrounds, highlighting nearby Seyfert galaxies as key targets for future high-energy observations to test this scenario.
AI.motivation: To clarify the uncertain origins of the cosmic neutrino background (CNB) and cosmic gamma-ray background (CGB), particularly assessing the contribution of AGN-driven accretion disk winds.
AI.method: A lepto-hadronic disk-wind model was constructed and calibrated using radio and GeV gamma-ray data from nearby Fermi-LAT-detected Seyfert galaxies, including constraints from recent XRISM observations. The model incorporated cosmic ray acceleration at wind-driven shocks producing various emissions and was applied to an AGN population synthesis model.
AI.result: Disk winds contribute at most approximately 5% of the CGB above 10 GeV and about 10% of the CNB around 100 TeV, indicating they are unlikely to dominate either background. Nearby Seyfert galaxies with ultrafast outflows are identified as promising observational targets for future high-energy gamma-ray and neutrino studies.
AI.conclusion: AGN accretion disk winds play only a minor role in generating the cosmic neutrino and gamma-ray backgrounds, and future observations of specific Seyfert galaxies can provide critical tests for the disk-wind origin scenario.

title: A rare sextuple-merging brightest cluster galaxy system in a disturbed galaxy cluster observed with the Einstein Probe Follow-up X-ray Telescope
comment: 7 pages, 6 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: The evolutionary processes of galaxy clusters influence the properties of their member galaxies. We present a joint X-ray--optical analysis of the galaxy cluster WHY J050106.2+013714 at $z_{\rm c}=0.151$. X-ray observations with the Einstein Probe Follow-up X-ray Telescope indicate that the cluster is dynamically young. The cluster displays an average X-ray temperature of $2.8^{+0.4}_{-0.3}$ keV and a total luminosity of 9.4$\pm0.3\times10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$, consistent with the scaling relation of typical disturbed clusters. Remarkably, the cluster hosts a multi-merging brightest cluster galaxy (BCG) system composed of six massive galaxies, with a total stellar mass of $1.16\times10^{12}M_{\odot}$. We detected a well-defined intracluster light component extending to a size of 310 kpc. A systematic search for merging BCGs in the DESI Legacy Surveys reveals that this sextuple-merging BCG is extremely rare in the local Universe. Additionally, other merging BCGs are also likely to form in moderately disturbed clusters, which provides valuable insights into the formation of BCGs.

AI.tldr: A detailed X-ray and optical study of cluster WHY J050106.2+013714 reveals it is dynamically young and uniquely hosts six merging massive BCGs, highlighting rare formation scenarios for brightest cluster galaxies in disturbed clusters.
AI.motivation: To understand how the evolutionary processes of galaxy clusters impact the properties and formation mechanisms of their member galaxies, particularly the brightest cluster galaxies.
AI.method: A joint X-ray and optical analysis was conducted using X-ray observations from the Einstein Probe Follow-up X-ray Telescope and optical data from the DESI Legacy Surveys to study the cluster's properties and search for merging BCGs.
AI.result: The cluster shows typical disturbed cluster characteristics with an average X-ray temperature of ~2.8 keV and luminosity consistent with disturbed clusters. It hosts a rare BCG system formed by six merging massive galaxies with a large stellar mass and an extended intracluster light component. Other merging BCGs are also found in moderately disturbed clusters, suggesting common formation pathways.
AI.conclusion: The cluster WHY J050106.2+013714 is dynamically young and hosts a rare sextuple-merging brightest cluster galaxy system, providing unique insights into BCG formation in disturbed clusters.

title: Effects of Rotation on the Gravitational Tug-Boat Mechanism for Neutron-Star Kicks and Implications for Spin-Kick Alignment
comment: Submitted to PASA
summary: Neutron stars are often born with large recoil velocities, or natal kicks, whose physical origin remains an open question in core-collapse supernova theory. One possible mechanism is the gravitational tug-boat effect, in which anisotropic ejecta gravitationally accelerate the proto-neutron star over a timescale of seconds after shock revival. Observations suggest that the spin-kick angle distribution is not isotropic but skewed toward spin-kick alignment. Previous derivations of the tug-boat mechanism do not include the effect of initial stellar rotation. Here we derive a minimalist extension to assess how rotation of the expanding asymmetric mass distribution influences the spin-kick alignment. We show that the spin-kick angle is determined by the product of two factors, one that depends on the ratio of shock expansion time to the rotation period and the other which depends on the orientation of the asymmetric mass distribution with respect to the spin-axis. For fast enough rotation, the first factor amounts to axially averaging out non-axisymmetry thereby suppressing the perpendicular tug and leaving only a spin-aligned force. However, the rotation speed required for this effect would be unrealistically large unless magnetic fields could transport angular momentum from the core to the outflow efficiently. Otherwise, spin-kick alignment for the tug-boat mechanism would be more likely achieved via the second factor, namely for systems in which the mass flux asymmetry is itself preferentially spin-aligned.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the gravitational tug-boat model of neutron star natal kicks by including stellar rotation, finding that realistic rotation speeds are too low to cause spin-kick alignment through rotational averaging; instead, alignment likely arises from spin-aligned asymmetries in mass ejection.
AI.motivation: To address the open question of the physical origin of natal kicks in neutron stars and explain observed spin-kick angle distributions that favor spin-kick alignment, extending previous models that neglected initial stellar rotation effects.
AI.method: A minimalist theoretical extension was derived to include the influence of initial stellar rotation on the gravitational tug-boat effect, analyzing how rotation modulates the spin-kick angle through the ratio of shock expansion time to rotation period and the orientation of asymmetric ejecta relative to the spin axis.
AI.result: The analysis shows that for fast rotation, non-axisymmetric ejecta effects average out, leading to spin-aligned kicks, but the rotation speed required is unrealistically high without magnetic angular momentum transport. Therefore, observed spin-kick alignment likely results from the intrinsic alignment of asymmetric mass ejection with the spin axis rather than rotation-induced averaging.
AI.conclusion: Spin-kick alignment in neutron stars via the gravitational tug-boat mechanism is influenced by rotational effects, but realistic rotation speeds are generally insufficient to produce alignment unless aided by efficient magnetic angular momentum transport. Spin-kick alignment is thus more likely due to intrinsic spin-aligned asymmetries in mass ejection rather than rotation averaging effects.

title: Alleviating the Hubble tension with the $Λ_{ω_s}$CDM model
comment: Proceeding AstroMarche2 conference, September 2025, Accepted for publication in IJMPA, 7 pages, 2 figures, 1 table
summary: We formulate a novel extension of the $Λ$CDM model, named $Λ_{ω_s}$CDM, in which we consider an additional term at early times in order to alleviate the Hubble tension. This additional component, referred to as \emph{matter with pressure}, indicates a barotropic fluid that is subdominant to dust and radiation as the Universe expands, thereby recovering the $Λ$CDM paradigm at late times. We constrain the $Λ_{ω_s}$CDM cosmology by performing a Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis with Planck 2018 CMB, DESI DR2, and Pantheon+\texttt{SH0ES} data. The results suggest that the barotropic factor and the normalized density of the new fluid are given, respectively, by $ω_s=0.294_{-0.004(0.023)}^{+0.014(0.015)}$ and $10^{5}Ω_s=1.62_{-0.56(0.91)}^{+0.36(1.02)}$. With these two additional parameters, the Hubble constant is increased to $H_0 = 71.51^{+0.72(1.43)}_{-0.74(1.46)}$ km/s/Mpc, alleviating \emph{de facto} the Hubble tension.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the Λ_{ω_s}CDM model by adding a barotropic fluid component at early times to the ΛCDM cosmology, which raises the Hubble constant estimate and eases the Hubble tension, validated by recent cosmological observations.
AI.motivation: To alleviate the Hubble tension observed in cosmological measurements by extending the standard ΛCDM model with an additional early-time component.
AI.method: Formulation of a novel cosmological model called Λ_{ω_s}CDM including a barotropic fluid with pressure as an additional term at early times, and constraining the model using Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis on Planck 2018 CMB, DESI DR2, and Pantheon+SH0ES data.
AI.result: The parameters of the new fluid were constrained to a barotropic factor ω_s≈0.294 and normalized density Ω_s≈1.62×10^{-5}, leading to an increased Hubble constant value H_0≈71.51 km/s/Mpc, effectively alleviating the Hubble tension.
AI.conclusion: The Λ_{ω_s}CDM model incorporating a subdominant barotropic fluid at early times successfully increases the Hubble constant estimate, thus providing a viable resolution to the Hubble tension while recovering the standard ΛCDM behavior at late times.

title: A MUSE View of the Optical Torus within the Supernova Remnant 1E 0102.2-7219
comment: 19 pages, 13 figures, 3 tables; Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We present new MUSE Narrow Field Mode with Adaptive Optics observations of the optical torus surrounding a Central Compact Object (CCO) candidate within the oxygen-rich supernova remnant 1E 0102.2-7219 (E0102) located in the Small Magellanic Cloud. These data provide nearly an order-of-magnitude improvement in spatial resolution over previous MUSE Wide Field Mode observations. The improved spatial resolution resolved the previously identified torus into a cavity-like structure with a sharply defined inner edge and diffuse, outer filamentary substructure. The emission shows continuous velocity connectivity, broad intrinsic line widths, and co-spatial contributions from neutral and partially ionized species, including O I, Ne I, [O I], [O II], and [O III]. Spatially resolved line-ratio maps indicate that the emission arises from a multiphase, non-equilibrium medium rather than a single homogeneous component. Comparison with photoionization and shock models shows that no single-component model within the explored parameter space can simultaneously reproduce both the strong neutral and high-ionization diagnostics, indicating that multiple physical conditions must coexist. We favor an interpretation in which shocks propagating through density inhomogeneities in the ejecta shape the observed morphology and excitation, while also considering alternative mechanisms linked to the central source, binary evolution, or interaction with an embedded object within the remnant.

AI.tldr: High-resolution MUSE observations reveal that the optical torus around a CCO candidate in supernova remnant E0102 is a complex, multiphase structure shaped by shocks in inhomogeneous ejecta, challenging single-component interpretation models.
AI.motivation: To obtain higher spatial resolution observations of the optical torus around a CCO candidate in supernova remnant E0102, enabling better understanding of its detailed structure and physical conditions.
AI.method: Used the MUSE Narrow Field Mode with Adaptive Optics to achieve an order-of-magnitude improvement in spatial resolution over previous Wide Field Mode observations, allowing detailed spatial and spectral analysis of emission lines and morphology.
AI.result: Resolved the previously identified torus into a cavity-like structure with distinct inner edges and filamentary substructure; emission shows velocity connectivity and contributions from neutral and ionized species, indicating a multiphase, non-equilibrium medium that cannot be explained by single-component photoionization or shock models.
AI.conclusion: The observed morphology and excitation are best explained by shocks propagating through density inhomogeneities in the ejecta, though alternative explanations including effects from the central source, binary evolution, or embedded object interaction are also considered.

title: Two-population model of type Ia supernovae and their associations with host galaxies in ZTF DR2
comment: to be submitted to A&A; 14 pages, 7 figures, 1 table
summary: We constrain type Ia supernova intrinsic properties, extinction, and probabilistic supernova-host associations using the volume-limited sample from the Zwicky Transient Factory DR2, the largest selection-free data set of type Ia supernovae to date. We employ Bayesian hierarchical modelling to jointly analyse the distribution of SALT2 light-curve parameters and global host-galaxy properties (stellar mass and rest-frame g-z colour). The adopted model is a mixture of distributions representing two supernova populations corresponding to two distinct modes of the stretch-parameter distribution, and two host-galaxy populations corresponding to two modes in the host-galaxy parameter space (red/massive and blue/less massive). Motivated by observations, high-stretch supernovae are allowed to populate both host-galaxy populations, whereas low-stretch supernovae are assumed to be exclusively associated with the red/massive host-galaxy population. The apparent non-linearity of the supernova magnitude-stretch relation implies a luminosity gap between the supernova populations, with the low-stretch population being Delta MB=0.14+/-0.03 mag brighter at x1=0, and different slopes (Delta alpha=0.064+/-0.023, steeper for the low-stretch population). The mean extinction coefficient is RB=3.89+/-0.29 (consistent with typical Milky Way values) in the blue/less massive host-galaxy population, which contains 68 per cent of high-stretch supernovae, and RB=3.08+/-0.08 in the red/massive host-galaxy population. Host-galaxy step corrections, both in stellar mass and colour, naturally emerge from the way the two supernova populations, characterised by different intrinsic luminosities and exctinctions, are distributed across host-galaxy populations. The adopted framework for modelling supernova populations and supernova-host associations makes host-galaxy step corrections redundant.

AI.tldr: This study uses Bayesian hierarchical modelling on a large Type Ia supernova data set to reveal two supernova populations tied to host-galaxy properties, explaining luminosity and extinction variations and making host-galaxy corrections unnecessary in cosmological analyses.
AI.motivation: The study aims to better understand intrinsic Type Ia supernova properties, extinction effects, and supernova-host galaxy associations using a large, selection-free data set to improve cosmological distance measurements.
AI.method: Bayesian hierarchical modelling was used to jointly analyze SALT2 light-curve parameters and host-galaxy properties within a mixture model representing dual supernova and host-galaxy populations.
AI.result: The analysis showed two supernova populations with different stretch-distribution modes, luminosity differences, extinction coefficients consistent with Milky Way values, and distinct host-galaxy associations, explaining observed luminosity and color step effects.
AI.conclusion: The paper concludes that modeling two distinct Type Ia supernova populations linked to different host-galaxy types naturally explains observed host-galaxy step corrections and removes the need for additional corrections in supernova cosmology.

title: A catalogue of TeV pulsar environments
comment: 11 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables, accepted for publication in Astronomy&Astrophysics
summary:
Pulsars and their environments represent a major class of Galactic gamma-ray sources. Their complex evolution, shaped by the interactions of the pulsar outflow with the supernova remnant (SNR) and the surrounding interstellar medium (ISM), produces diverse morphological and spectral characteristics observable from radio to PeV energies.
  This work collects and homogenizes data from all major operating TeV observatories, presenting the first comprehensive catalogue of TeV gamma-ray properties of pulsar environments.The catalogue is created from information regarding all gamma-ray sources that have been classified as pulsar-associated sources in published results from H.E.S.S., MAGIC, VERITAS, HAWC, and LHAASO. For each source, the observed gamma-ray properties are cross-matched with pulsar properties from the ATNF catalogue and Fermi-LAT pulsar catalogue.
  The final catalogue comprises all currently known TeV sources associated with pulsars, spanning all evolutionary stages. The sample consists of 128 gamma-ray sources, connected to 66 different pulsars. It reflects that the TeV-detected population is dominated by young and energetic pulsars located near the Galactic plane, but includes a growing number of middle-aged systems detected as extended halos. Only a weak correlation is found between TeV luminosity and pulsar characteristic age, indicating that TeV evolution is driven by environmental and transport effects rather than by spin-down age alone. Additionally, 5 pulsars which should host a PWN detectable by CTAO are identified as prime targets for future observation to improve our understanding of properties inhibiting the formation of a TeV nebula.
  This publicly available catalogue provides a uniform foundation for future population studies and for constraining models of particle transport and energy losses in pulsar environments.

AI.tldr: This work presents the first comprehensive catalogue of TeV gamma-ray properties for pulsar environments, integrating data from all major observatories and pulsar catalogues, revealing population characteristics and guiding future observational targets.
AI.motivation: To understand the gamma-ray properties and evolution of pulsar environments by compiling comprehensive data across major TeV observatories.
AI.method: Collected and homogenized observational data from H.E.S.S., MAGIC, VERITAS, HAWC, and LHAASO on pulsar-associated gamma-ray sources; cross-matched these with pulsar data from ATNF and Fermi-LAT catalogues to create a uniform catalogue.
AI.result: Produced the first extensive catalogue of 128 TeV gamma-ray sources linked to 66 pulsars, revealing that young, energetic pulsars dominate the TeV-detected population near the Galactic plane, with middle-aged pulsars appearing as extended halos. Found a weak correlation between TeV luminosity and pulsar age, suggesting environmental and transport effects influence TeV evolution more than spin-down age. Identified 5 prime pulsars for future observation with CTAO.
AI.conclusion: The catalogue serves as a uniform resource for future population studies and model constraints related to particle transport and energy losses in pulsar environments, advancing understanding of pulsar outflow interactions in the Galaxy.

title: Data-Driven Discovery of a Simple Phantom-Crossing Dark Energy Parametrization
comment: 30 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables. Comments welcome!
summary: We develop a data-driven reconstruction programme for the dark-energy equation of state within VCDM, a minimally modified gravity framework in which both background and linear perturbations can be consistently evolved across the phantom divide. Using CMB, BAO, and type-Ia supernova data, we first perform a Bayesian spline reconstruction of $w(a)$, finding a preference for smooth, monotonic phantom-crossing trajectories. Bayesian evidence disfavors increasingly complex spline models, indicating that current observations exhibit a statistical preference for low-complexity dark-energy dynamics. Motivated by this result, we apply Exhaustive Symbolic Regression, an interpretable machine-learning technique that systematically searches over analytic expressions of fixed complexity, identifying the remarkably simple one-parameter form $w(a)={w_0}/{\sqrt a}$, which reproduces the reconstructed behaviour and fits the data at a level comparable to standard two-parameter parametrizations such as CPL. The model naturally crosses the phantom divide for $w_0<0$, suppresses early dark energy, and predicts a transient accelerating and phantom phase without a future big-rip singularity. As a one-parameter model, it is highly predictive, being a genuinely dynamical deformation of the cosmological constant rather than containing it as a limit. Bayesian model comparison yields mild-to-moderate support for this parametrization relative to standard two-parameter alternatives, and stronger evidence relative to $Λ$CDM. Our results suggest that current observations favour surprisingly simple dark-energy dynamics and illustrate how Bayesian reconstruction and symbolic regression can be combined into a principled model-discovery framework for cosmology.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a Bayesian and machine-learning framework to reconstruct the dark-energy equation of state in a modified gravity context, discovering a simple one-parameter model that fits cosmological data well and is favored over more complex and standard models.
AI.motivation: To reconstruct the dark-energy equation of state within the VCDM minimally modified gravity framework, allowing consistent evolution across the phantom divide and to explore simpler, interpretable models favored by data complexity criteria.
AI.method: The study employs Bayesian spline reconstruction to model the dark-energy equation of state, followed by Exhaustive Symbolic Regression to identify a simple analytic form. Data from CMB, BAO, and type-Ia supernovae are used for Bayesian model comparison.
AI.result: Identification of a simple one-parameter form $w(a)={w_0}/{\sqrt a}$ that fits observational data comparably to standard two-parameter models, naturally crosses the phantom divide, suppresses early dark energy, predicts transient acceleration without big-rip singularity, and receives Bayesian support over $\Lambda$CDM and other parametrizations.
AI.conclusion: Current observational data favor surprisingly simple dark-energy dynamics characterized by a one-parameter equation of state that crosses the phantom divide smoothly and monotonically, challenging more complex models and standard parametrizations.

title: Effective description of lensed gravitational waves diffracted by stellar fields
comment: 17 pages, 9 figures. Comments welcome!
summary: As natural telescopes, Gravitational lenses enable the observation of sources that would otherwise be too distant and faint. Stellar-mass objects, or microlenses, act as impurities in the lens, producing subtle distortions of the source. These effects are necessary to correctly interpret observations, and may in some cases be themselves evidence of gravitational magnification. Gravitational waves (GWs) observed by ground detectors and magnified by galaxies and clusters will undergo microlensing by fields of stars and remnants: describing these systems requires not only considering a large number of small-scale lenses (microlenses), but also including wave-optics effects, leading to frequency dependent modulations of the signal. Here we present novel models for Reduced-Order Stochastic Diffraction (ROSD), which overcome these challenges in the search for GW lensing signatures: an effective description is synthesized from numerical simulations of wave-optics lensing by stellar fields via a singular value decomposition. The procedure yields an optimized orthonormal basis to describe microlensing distortions and a probability density function for the coefficients, which can be used as priors or to verify the consistency with stellar-field lensing. We present SVD-stellar-I5-aLIGO as an example of this model category, discuss the role of truncation order and demonstrate how it can be applied to GW data via injection and recovery in Bayesian parameter estimation. ROSD can be tailored to account for detector sensitivity and the type of source under analysis, and extended to different microlens populations and external potentials. ROSD models open a new window to probe small-scale objects (stars, remnants and potentially dark matter) and facilitate the discovery of the most distant compact binary mergers.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces ROSD models using singular value decomposition to effectively model microlensing effects on gravitational waves, facilitating accurate detection and analysis of lensing signatures from stellar fields and enhancing the study of distant compact binary mergers.
AI.motivation: Gravitational waves magnified by galaxies and clusters are subject to microlensing by stellar fields, producing subtle signal distortions that need to be accurately described, including wave-optics frequency-dependent modulations, in order to correctly interpret observations and detect lensing signatures.
AI.method: The method involves synthesizing an effective description from numerical simulations of wave-optics lensing by stellar fields using singular value decomposition to generate an optimized orthonormal basis and a probability density function for coefficients representing microlensing distortions.
AI.result: The paper presents ROSD models, exemplified by SVD-stellar-I5-aLIGO, demonstrates the impact of truncation order, and shows their applicability in Bayesian parameter estimation for gravitational wave data, with flexibility to adapt to different detector sensitivities, source types, microlens populations, and external potentials.
AI.conclusion: Reduced-Order Stochastic Diffraction (ROSD) models provide an effective and computationally feasible method to describe microlensing effects on gravitational waves, including wave-optics effects, enabling the identification and interpretation of lensing signatures in GW observations.

title: Weak-lensing mass calibration of \emph{Planck} Sunyaev--Zel'dovich clusters with HSC-SSP Year~3
comment: 27 pages, 10 figures, submitted to PRD
summary: We present a weak gravitational lensing mass calibration of 19 \textit{Planck} Sunyaev--Zel'dovich (SZ) selected galaxy clusters using shape measurements from the Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program (HSC-SSP) Year 3 shape catalog. We measure the stacked weak-lensing signal $ΔΣ(R)$ using per-cluster lensing weights that match the measurement pipeline's stacking scheme, and construct an analytical covariance matrix that includes shape noise and projected large-scale structure contributions. Our primary constraint on the SZ mass bias comes from a forward-modeling approach that integrates over the halo mass function while accounting for the \textit{Planck} SZ selection function, Eddington bias from log-normal scatter in the SZ mass proxy, and cluster miscentering. Fitting four free parameters, the log mass bias $\ln(1-b)$, the miscentered fraction $f_{\rm mis}$, the offset scale $σ_{\rm off}$, and the SZ scatter $σ_{\ln M}$, over the radial range $0.5$--$5.0\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, we obtain $1-b = 0.73^{+0.10}_{-0.11}$ with $χ^2/\mathrm{dof} = 5.2/5$ at an effective redshift $z_{\rm eff}\simeq 0.24$. This measurement is consistent with recent weak-lensing calibrations of SZ-selected clusters and supports the picture that significant mass bias corrections are required to reconcile cluster abundance measurements with primary cosmic microwave background constraints on cosmological parameters.

AI.tldr: Weak lensing analysis of 19 Planck SZ clusters using HSC-SSP data shows the cluster masses are biased low by about 27%, consistent with other studies, which supports the need for mass bias corrections to reconcile cluster and CMB cosmology.
AI.motivation: Accurate mass calibration of galaxy clusters selected by the Planck SZ effect is crucial to reconcile cluster abundance measurements with cosmological constraints from the cosmic microwave background (CMB).
AI.method: Performed a weak gravitational lensing analysis of 19 Planck SZ-selected clusters using HSC-SSP Year 3 shape data, measuring the stacked lensing signal with per-cluster weights, constructing an analytical covariance including shape noise and large-scale structure, and applying a forward-modeling approach incorporating the Planck SZ selection function, Eddington bias, and cluster miscentering. Four parameters (log mass bias, miscentered fraction, offset scale, SZ scatter) were fitted over 0.5 to 5 Mpc scale.
AI.result: The log mass bias parameter was constrained to $1-b = 0.73^{+0.10}_{-0.11}$ at an effective redshift of 0.24 with good fit quality ($chi^2/	ext{dof}=5.2/5$). This result aligns with recent weak-lensing calibrations and implies significant mass bias corrections are necessary for consistency between cluster counts and primary CMB cosmological measurements.
AI.conclusion: Weak lensing calibration confirms that Planck SZ cluster masses are biased low and significant correction is needed to align cluster abundance data with cosmological parameters from the CMB.

title: An atypical X-ray variability component in the black hole candidate AT2019wey
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures, Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Recent studies have revealed a notable timing feature in several black hole X-ray binaries (BHXBs) during the soft-to-hard transition at the outburst decay. Within a narrow frequency range, the phase lags between high- and low-energy X-ray light curves exhibit a sudden increase, accompanied by a drop in the coherence function. These narrow features have been associated with a quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO) appearing only in the imaginary part of the cross spectrum (CS). This QPO remains undetected in the power density spectrum (PDS) and is known as imaginary QPO. Motivated by these results, we analyse five years of NICER observations of the BHXB AT2019wey during its low-hard state (LHS) and hard-intermediate state (HIMS). We find an imaginary QPO in the CS of AT2019wey, with similar characteristics as those found in other BHXBs, making AT2019wey the fifth BHXB in which such QPOs have been found. As the source hardens, the frequency of the imaginary QPO drops from $\sim$ 5 Hz to $\sim$ 1 Hz, while its phase lag rises from $\sim$ 0.3 rad to $\sim$ 0.7 rad during the HIMS and from $\sim$ 0.5 rad to $\sim$ 0.6 rad during the LHS. During the HIMS, the phase-lag energy spectrum of the imaginary QPO shows a typical U-shaped profile, while the shape changes in the LHS. The rms spectrum of the imaginary QPO rises below $\sim$ 2 keV, peaks at around $\sim$ 2 keV and decreases at higher energies, which may be associated with the presence of a relatively cool corona. We compare the properties of the imaginary QPO with those of the type-B and C QPOs in BHXBs and find a tentative connection to type-C QPOs. Combining the imaginary QPOs detected in AT2019wey with those reported in other sources, we find a systematic increase of QPO phase lags with QPO frequency. However, we cannot conclude whether the phase lags of imaginary QPOs exhibit the inclination dependence previously observed in type-C QPOs.

AI.tldr: This study reports the detection of an imaginary QPO in the black hole X-ray binary AT2019wey, showing characteristic frequency, phase lag, and spectral behaviors similar to previously known imaginary QPOs, suggesting a connection to type-C QPOs and contributing to understanding timing features in BHXBs during state transitions.
AI.motivation: To investigate the newly noted imaginary QPOs in black hole X-ray binaries and their properties in the source AT2019wey, motivated by previous findings of these QPOs in other BHXBs during state transitions.
AI.method: Analyzed five years of NICER X-ray timing observations of AT2019wey during its low-hard and hard-intermediate states, focusing on the cross spectrum and phase lag behaviors associated with the imaginary QPO.
AI.result: Detected an imaginary QPO in AT2019wey similar to other BHXBs, with frequency decreasing from ~5 Hz to ~1 Hz as the source hardens; phase lags increased and showed distinct energy dependence across states, with rms spectra suggesting a cool corona; found tentative links to type-C QPOs and systematic phase lag increase with QPO frequency across sources.
AI.conclusion: Imaginary QPOs are confirmed in AT2019wey, exhibiting consistent characteristics with those in other BHXBs, likely related to type-C QPOs, although inclination dependence of phase lags remains inconclusive.

title: Constraints on the Sum of Neutrino Masses from ACT DR6 and DESI DR2 Considering Isocurvature Initial Conditions
comment: 13 pages, 6 figures
summary: We present a robust assessment of cosmological constraints on the sum of neutrino masses ($\sum m_ν$) when relaxing the standard assumption of purely adiabatic primordial initial conditions. Allowing for a neutrino density isocurvature (NDI) component alongside the adiabatic mode, we analyse the latest CMB-SPA combination (Planck 2018, ACT DR6, and SPT-3G), DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation data, and the DES Year 5 supernova sample. Within the $Λ$CDM model, the 95\% upper limit weakens only marginally from $\sum m_ν< 0.052$ eV (purely adiabatic) to $< 0.057$ eV (including NDI), with the NDI amplitude consistent with zero. In the CPL dynamical dark energy model, the adiabatic limit is $< 0.111$ eV, shifting to $< 0.115$ eV with NDI, yet the isocurvature mode remains undetected.
